challenges.name: moves-copies-and-clones-quiz
challenges.title: Moves, copies and clones
challenges.description: Decide which values are moved, which are copied, and which programs the borrow checker accepts.

questions.explanation: Line (E): error[E0382]: borrow of moved value: `route`. Passing route to ship at (B) moves the String into the function's parameter, and the String is dropped when ship returns, so main may not use route afterwards. Line (B) itself is fine: moving a value into a function is allowed, it only ends main's ownership. Line (C) is fine because u32 is a Copy type: let total = parcels copies the number, and both variables stay usable. Line (D) prints the usize that ship returned, which main owns. The program would compile if (E) were removed, or if ship were called with route.clone().

options.text: (A), because parcels is moved into total
(B), because a String cannot be passed to a function by value
(E), because route was moved into ship at (B)

questions.question: Each option is the body of main in a program compiled with rustc --edition 2024, which also contains fn take(s: String) -> String { s }. Which of them compile? (Select all that apply.)
questions.explanation: a.clone() makes a second, independent String, so a and b both own their own text and can both be printed. A &str such as "DN-07" is a Copy type (copying it copies a reference to text that lives for the whole program), so b = a leaves a usable. take(a) moves a into the function and the function gives the String back; let a = take(a) binds the returned String to a new a, so printing it is fine. The tuple (3_u8, String) is NOT Copy because one of its parts, the String, is not Copy: b = a moves the whole tuple and printing a is error[E0382]: borrow of moved value: `a`. for x in v consumes the vector (it calls into_iter, which takes ownership), so v.len() afterwards is error[E0382] too; for x in &v would borrow it instead.

challenges.name: fix-cage-manifest-clones
challenges.title: Fix the cage manifest that cloned its way to compiling
challenges.description: The cage manifest tool compiles, but bags never show up on the manifest, a parcel scanned twice in one bag is listed twice, and after a merge the parcels appear in both cages. add_bag and merge were written by adding .clone() until the compiler stopped complaining, so they change copies and return the wrong values. Fix both functions so they take ownership of the cages they are given, change them, and give the right ones back. The test runner reads bag and merge commands and prints every cage at the end.

tests.name: Example from the task: a double beep and a merge
tests.input:
bag DN-07 SH-1001 SH-1002
bag DN-07 SH-1003 SH-1003
bag DN-08 SH-2001
merge DN-08 DN-07
tests.expected:
DN-07: 4 parcels [SH-1001, SH-1002, SH-1003, SH-2001]
DN-08: 0 parcels []

tests.name: Two bags into one cage, a parcel re-scanned in the second bag
After a merge the source cage is empty
tests.input:
bag DN-03 SH-4001
bag DN-05 SH-5001 SH-5002
merge DN-05 DN-03
tests.expected:
DN-03: 3 parcels [SH-4001, SH-5001, SH-5002]
DN-05: 0 parcels []

tests.name: A parcel scanned into both cages is listed once after the merge
tests.input:
bag DN-07 SH-6001 SH-6002
bag DN-09 SH-6002 SH-6003 SH-6003
merge DN-09 DN-07
bag DN-09 SH-6004
tests.expected:
DN-07: 3 parcels [SH-6001, SH-6002, SH-6003]
DN-09: 1 parcels [SH-6004]

tests.name: Chained merges into an empty cage keep first-scan order
tests.input:
bag DN-01 SH-7001 SH-7002
bag DN-02 SH-7003
merge DN-01 DN-04
merge DN-02 DN-04
bag DN-01 SH-7001
bag DN-04 SH-7001 SH-7005
tests.expected:
DN-01: 1 parcels [SH-7001]
DN-02: 0 parcels []
DN-04: 4 parcels [SH-7001, SH-7002, SH-7003, SH-7005]
